study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual differences v. the average patient: mapping the heterogeneity in ADHD using normative models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify and map brain structural heterogeneity in adults with persistent ADHD at the individual patient level using normative modeling, and to investigate the degree of spatial overlap in terms of deviations from the normative model to provide concrete estimates for disorder heterogeneity.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score with threshold |Z| > 2.6 for extreme deviations; percentage of extreme positive (Z > 2.6) and extreme negative (Z < -2.6) deviations; voxel-wise overlap maps
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The paper clearly describes using Z-scores computed for each voxel reflecting the difference between predicted and true volume normalized by prediction uncertainty. Extreme deviations were defined as |Z| > 2.6, with separate thresholds for positive (Z > 2.6) and negative (Z < -2.6) deviations. Percentage scores were computed for each participant, and voxel-wise overlap was calculated.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: We were able to statistically quantify deviations from the normative model with regional specificity, by computing a Z-score for each voxel, reflecting the difference between the predicted volume and the true volume normalized by the uncertainty of the prediction... Next, the individual maps of deviation were thresholded at |Z| > 2.6... Extreme positive deviations were defined as all voxels with a value higher than Z > 2.6, while extreme negative deviations are defined as a value below the Z < -2.6. All extreme deviations were combined into scores representing the percentage of extreme positive and extreme negative deviations for each participant.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group-level deviations analyzed using PALM (Permutation Analysis of Linear Model) with permutation-based inference and threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE), FDR corrected at 5%; group comparisons of extreme deviation percentages using nonparametric χ² test in a general linear model with Bonferroni-Holm correction; voxel-wise overlap analysis between individuals; associations between percentage of extreme deviations and age, symptom scores (hyperactivity/impulsivity, inattention from DIVA), stimulant medication, and comorbidity tested in ADHD group with Bonferroni-Holm correction (correcting for 8 correlations and modality).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: At the group level, participants with ADHD showed significantly reduced gray matter in cerebellum, hippocampus, and temporal regions compared to healthy individuals, and significantly higher percentages of extreme negative deviations in both gray and white matter; however, at the individual level, extreme deviations showed marked heterogeneity with overlap in more than 2% of ADHD participants observed only in few brain loci (primarily cerebellum, hippocampus, basal ganglia), demonstrating substantial inter-individual variation.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Group-level analyses revealed that participants with ADHD showed mean deviations from the normative model that were significantly different from healthy individuals (FDR corrected at 5%) in cerebellar regions, temporal regions, and hippocampus. When examining extreme deviations, participants with persistent ADHD showed significantly higher percentages of extreme negative deviations in gray matter (0.48%; 95% CI 0.30-0.66%) compared to healthy individuals (0.28%; 95% CI 0.24-0.34%; Wald χ²(1)=23.64, p<0.001 corrected). Similarly, in white matter, ADHD participants showed 0.41% (95% CI 0.24-0.57%) extreme negative deviations compared to 0.24% (95% CI 0.17-0.31%) in healthy individuals (Wald χ²(1)=18.02, p<0.001 corrected). No significant differences were observed in positive deviations. At the individual level, overlap analysis revealed that more than 2% of participants with ADHD showed extreme negative deviations primarily in the cerebellum, hippocampus, and basal ganglia; however, overall spatial overlap was limited, with nine out of ten most negatively deviating patients showing extreme values in the cerebellum but in non-overlapping areas. Individual deviation patterns were largely unique for each participant. The extreme negative deviations in white matter were associated with age in ADHD participants (β=0.198, p=0.014 uncorrected), but no associations survived correction for multiple comparisons with symptom scores, stimulant medication, or comorbidity.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small sample size requiring 10-fold cross-validation in healthy individuals rather than independent train/test split, potentially introducing small bias; symptom scores based on self-report which are noisier than diagnostic interviews; insufficient sample to inspect effects of comorbidities and confounding factors due to inconsistency across individuals; single-site study limiting generalizability
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, we had to use 10-fold cross-validation in healthy individuals and out of sample predictions in individuals with persistent ADHD, as our healthy sample was too small to split it into two. This potentially introduces a small bias. Second, we did not find associations of symptom scores with the percentage of deviation from the normative model. However, the measures we used to assess symptoms rely on self-report, which is generally noisier than measures from diagnostic interviews. Finally, our sample did not allow to inspect the effect of comorbidities and other potentially confounding factors on the obtained results as the comorbidities were inconsistent across individuals.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study employed sex-stratified normative modeling (modeling females and males separately) due to sex effects in ADHD. Individual deviation maps were also analyzed using FDR correction at the individual participant level (Benjamini-Hochberg procedure), which did not change conclusions. The authors note that larger, more representative samples capture more biological and procedural heterogeneity, which may explain why predictive accuracy decreases in larger ADHD studies contrary to typical machine learning expectations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a seminal paper demonstrating the application of normative modeling to psychiatric disorders, specifically highlighting the concept of biological heterogeneity and questioning the validity of the 'average patient' concept. The study is limited to a single site (Radboud University Medical Center, 1.5T Siemens Avanto scanner). Age range covers adult lifespan (approximately 20-70 years based on figures). The normative model showed global gray matter decreases with age (20-70 years) with largest decreases in frontal and cerebellar regions, while white matter showed both increases (parietal/temporal) and decreases (frontal/thalamic) with age, consistent with healthy aging literature. Exclusion criteria for ADHD participants included psychosis, substance use disorder, IQ<70, neurological disorders, sensorimotor disabilities, and medication other than psychostimulants or atomoxetine. At time of scanning, 11.8% of ADHD participants were currently on stimulant medication, 76.4% had past use, and 11.8% had no medication history.
